classes.name: average daily earnings
classes.label: average daily earnings
classes.definition: measure of the average daily wage an employee makes over the reporting period

classes.name: average earnings
classes.label: average earnings
classes.definition: measure of the average wage an hourly or salaried worker makes in a given period of time

classes.name: average hourly earnings
classes.label: average hourly earnings
classes.definition: measure of the average hourly wage an employee makes over the reporting period

classes.name: average monthly earnings
classes.label: average monthly earnings
classes.definition: measure of the average monthly wage an employee makes over the reporting period

classes.name: average weekly earnings
classes.label: average weekly earnings
classes.definition: measure of the average weekly wage an employee makes over the reporting period

classes.name: capital-labor-energy-materials multifactor productivity
classes.label: capital-labor-energy-materials multifactor productivity
classes.definition: ratio of a quantity index of gross output to a quantity index of combined inputs

classes.name: capital-labor multifactor productivity (MFP), based on value added
classes.label: capital-labor multifactor productivity (MFP), based on value added
classes.definition: ratio of a quantity index of value added to a quantity index of combined labor and capital input

classes.name: capital productivity, based on value added
classes.label: capital productivity, based on value added
classes.definition: ratio of a quantity index of value added to a quantity index of capital input

classes.name: civilian
classes.label: civilian
classes.definition: person that is not a member of the military (i.e., that is not on active duty)

classes.name: civilian labor force
classes.label: civilian labor force
classes.definition: subset of the civilian, non-institutional population considered to be part of the labor force during a given reporting period

classes.name: civilian labor force participation rate
classes.label: civilian labor force participation rate
classes.definition: economic indicator representing the rate of participation the labor force of a given economy for some specified period

classes.name: civilian non-institutional person
classes.label: civilian non-institutional person
classes.definition: legal working-age person that does not live in an institution (for example, a correctional facility, long-term care hospital, or nursing home), and is not on active military duty

classes.name: civilian non-institutional population
classes.label: civilian non-institutional population
classes.definition: statistical universe consisting of people of a certain age who reside in a given region, do not live in institutions (for example, correctional facilities, long-term care hospitals, and nursing homes), and are not on active military duty

classes.name: combined statistical area
classes.label: combined statistical area
classes.definition: combination of adjacent metropolitan and micropolitan areas with economic ties measured by commuting patterns

classes.name: consumer price index
classes.label: consumer price index
classes.definition: economic indicator representing measure of the change over time in the prices of consumer goods and services that households consume

classes.name: discouraged worker population
classes.label: discouraged worker population
classes.definition: subset of the marginally attached population that have given a job-market related reason for not currently looking for work

classes.name: economic indicator
classes.label: economic indicator
classes.definition: statistical measure of economic activity that is regular and comparable in the context of a statistical area (region), used for analysis of economic performance and predictions of future performance

classes.name: employed population
classes.label: employed population
classes.definition: subset of the civilian labor force considered to be employed during the reporting period

classes.name: employed population part-time
classes.label: employed population part-time
classes.definition: subset of the employed population that includes persons that are working fewer than 30 to 35 hours per week based on usual working hours

classes.name: employed population part-time for economic reasons
classes.label: employed population part-time for economic reasons
classes.definition: subset of the employed population that includes persons that are working fewer than 30 to 35 hours per week due to slack work, unfavorable business conditions, inability to find full-time work, and seasonal declines in demand

classes.name: employed population part-time for non-economic reasons
classes.label: employed population part-time for non-economic reasons
classes.definition: subset of the employed population that includes persons that are working fewer than 30 to 35 hours per week due to illness or other health or medical limitations, childcare problems, family or personal obligations, being in school or training, retirement or Social Security limits on earnings, and having a job where full-time work is less than 35 hours

classes.name: employed population temporarily not at work
classes.label: employed population temporarily not at work
classes.definition: subset of the employed population that includes persons that are temporarily absent from work for various reasons

classes.name: employment-population ratio
classes.label: employment-population ratio
classes.definition: economic indicator representing the ratio of the employed population with respect to the overall civilian non-institutional population of a given economy for some specified period

classes.name: enterprise
classes.label: enterprise
classes.definition: functional business entity that produces and/or sells goods or services

classes.name: enterprise population
classes.label: enterprise population
classes.definition: statistical universe consisting of enterprises designed for the purposes of supporting surveys such as those used as the basis for employment and producer price indices

classes.name: establishment
classes.label: establishment
classes.definition: an enterprise (or part of an enterprise) that operates from a single physical location

classes.name: establishment employment
classes.label: establishment employment
classes.definition: economic indicator representing the total number of persons who work in or for the establishment including working proprietors, active business partners and unpaid family workers, as well as persons working outside the establishment when paid by and under the control of the establishment, for example, sales representatives, outside service engineers and repair and maintenance personnel

classes.name: establishment population
classes.label: establishment population
classes.definition: a subset of the enterprise population focused on establishments

classes.name: fixed basket
classes.label: fixed basket
classes.definition: basket of goods and services whose quantity and quality are held fixed for some period of time

classes.name: fixed basket constituent
classes.label: fixed basket constituent
classes.definition: component of a fixed basket

classes.name: fixed basket population
classes.label: fixed basket population
classes.definition: statistical universe consisting of specific goods and/or services designed for the purposes of supporting surveys such as those used as the basis for price indices

classes.name: government-specified statistical area
classes.label: government-specified statistical area
classes.definition: statistical area defined by a government agency

classes.name: gross domestic product
classes.label: gross domestic product
classes.definition: economic indicator representing the broadest measure of aggregate economic activity, measuring the total unduplicated market value of all final goods and services produced within a statistical area in a period

classes.name: household
classes.label: household
classes.definition: individual or small group of persons who occupy a housing unit (such as a house or apartment) as their usual place of residence, who pool some, or all, of their income and wealth and who consume certain types of goods and services collectively, mainly housing and food

classes.name: housing unit
classes.label: housing unit
classes.definition: house, an apartment, a mobile home or trailer, a group of rooms, or a single room occupied as separate living quarters, or if vacant, intended for occupancy as separate living quarters

classes.name: inflation rate
classes.label: inflation rate
classes.definition: economic indicator representing a change in prices of goods and services for a specified period, for a given statistical area

classes.name: input producer price index
classes.label: input producer price index
classes.definition: economic indicator representing measure of the rate of change over time in the prices of inputs of goods and services purchased by the producer

classes.name: institutional person
classes.label: institutional person
classes.definition: person that resides in an institution for some reason, due, for example, to hospitalization, rehabilitation, or incarceration

classes.name: institutional unit
classes.label: institutional unit
classes.definition: party that is capable, in its own right, of owning assets, incurring liabilities, and engaging in economic activities and in transactions with other parties

classes.name: labor productivity, based on gross output
classes.label: labor productivity, based on gross output
classes.definition: ratio of a quantity index of gross output to a quantity index of labor input

classes.name: labor productivity, based on value added
classes.label: labor productivity, based on value added
classes.definition: ratio of a quantity index of value added to a quantity index of labor input

classes.name: marginally attached population
classes.label: marginally attached population
classes.definition: subset of the population that includes people who currently are neither working nor looking for work but indicate that they want and are available for a job and have looked for work sometime in the past 12 months
parents: population not in the labor force

classes.name: metropolitan statistical area
classes.label: metropolitan statistical area
classes.definition: one or more adjacent counties or county equivalents that have at least one urban core area of at least 50,000 population, plus adjacent territory that has a high degree of social and economic integration with the core as measured by commuting ties

classes.name: micropolitan statistical area
classes.label: micropolitan statistical area
classes.definition: one or more adjacent counties or county equivalents that have at least one urban core area of at least 10,000 population but less than 50,000, plus adjacent territory that has a high degree of social and economic integration with the core as measured by commuting ties

classes.name: military person
classes.label: military person
classes.definition: person that is a member of the active duty military

classes.name: output producer price index
classes.label: output producer price index
classes.definition: economic indicator representing measure of the rate of change over time in the prices of products sold as they leave the producer

classes.name: personal consumption expenditures
classes.label: personal consumption expenditures
classes.definition: economic indicator representing measure of the value of the goods and services purchased by, or on the behalf of, 'persons'

classes.name: population not in the labor force
classes.label: population not in the labor force
classes.definition: subset of the civilian, noninstitutional population, that is considered neither employed nor unemployed by the reporting agency during the reporting period

classes.name: producer price index
classes.label: producer price index
classes.definition: economic indicator representing measure of the rate of change over time in the prices of goods and services bought and sold by producers

classes.name: productivity
classes.label: productivity
classes.definition: economic indicator representing ratio of a volume measure of output to a volume measure of input use

classes.name: statistical information publisher
classes.label: statistical information publisher
classes.definition: publisher that packages and makes analytical and statistical data available

classes.name: ultimate consumer
classes.label: ultimate consumer
classes.definition: person that is the ultimate user of a good, product or service

classes.name: underemployed population
classes.label: underemployed population
classes.definition: subset of the employed population that includes persons employed part-time for economic reasons, who want and are available for full-time work but have had to settle for a part-time schedule

classes.name: underemployed population with respect to occupation
classes.label: underemployed population with respect to occupation
classes.definition: subset of the underemployed population that includes persons employed in a role that does not reflect their training and experience, excluding those that change careers

classes.name: underutilized population
classes.label: underutilized population
classes.definition: subset of the civilian non-institutional population that includes persons employed part-time for economic reasons, persons that are marginally attached to the labor force, and persons that are identified as unemployed

classes.name: unemployed population
classes.label: unemployed population
classes.definition: subset of the civilian labor force that is considered to have had no employment but was available for work, except for temporary illness, and had made specific efforts to find employment sometime during a specified period, during the reporting period

classes.name: unemployment rate
classes.label: unemployment rate
classes.definition: economic indicator representing the ratio of the unemployed population with respect to the civilian labor force of a given economy for some specified period

classes.name: value-added producer price index
classes.label: value-added producer price index
classes.definition: economic indicator representing a weighted average of the input and output producer price indices

classes.name: Canadian consumer price index
classes.label: Canadian consumer price index
classes.definition: economic indicator representing a measure of changes over time in the prices of a fixed basket of consumer goods and services that Canadian private households consume

classes.name: Canadian households consumers universe
classes.label: Canadian households consumers universe
classes.definition: a statistical universe consisting of all private households in Canada, with the exception of soldiers on military bases, people living on First Nations reserves, institutionalized persons, and households living in the rural areas of the three northern territories

classes.name: Canadian producer price index
classes.label: Canadian producer price index
classes.definition: an economic indicator representing a measure of the change over time in the prices of a fixed-basket of domestic producer goods and services

classes.name: industrial products sector
classes.label: industrial products sector
classes.definition: a classifier for a sector of the economy used for price indices focused on major commodities sold by manufacturers in Canada

classes.name: new housing sector
classes.label: new housing sector
classes.definition: a classifier for a sector of the economy used for price indices focused on contractors' selling prices of new residential houses, where detailed specifications pertaining to each house remain the same between two consecutive periods

classes.name: raw materials sector
classes.label: raw materials sector
classes.definition: a classifier used for price indices related to raw materials purchased by industries in Canada for further processing

classes.name: American statistics publisher
classes.label: American statistics publisher
classes.definition: statistical information publisher comprised of the government agencies and departments that publish statistical information on behalf of the U.S. Federal Government

classes.name: consumer expenditure survey
classes.label: consumer expenditure survey
classes.definition: statistical program conducted on a regular basis that provides information on the buying habits of consumers, including data on their expenditures, income, and consumer unit (families and single consumers) characteristics

classes.name: current employment statistics
classes.label: current employment statistics
classes.definition: survey conducted on a regular basis that presents analytical information related to businesses and government agencies, in order to provide detailed industry data on employment, hours, and earnings of workers

classes.name: current population survey
classes.label: current population survey
classes.definition: survey conducted on a regular basis that presents analytical information related to the general population of a given statistical area with respect to labor force, employment, unemployment, persons not in the labor force, hours of work, earnings, and other demographic and labor force characteristics

classes.name: employment situation establishment survey
classes.label: employment situation establishment survey
classes.definition: survey conducted on a regular basis that presents analytical information related to the labor force of a given statistical area, surveyed with respect to businesses, and is, for the most part, seasonally adjusted

classes.name: employment situation household survey
classes.label: employment situation household survey
classes.definition: a survey conducted on a regular basis that presents analytical information related to the labor force of a given statistical area, surveyed with respect to households, and is, for the most part, seasonally adjusted

classes.name: employment situation survey
classes.label: employment situation survey
classes.definition: a survey conducted on a regular basis that presents analytical information focused on the employment characteristics of a given statistical area

classes.name: point of purchase survey
classes.label: point of purchase survey
classes.definition: a program conducted on a regular basis that provides information on purchases of various items and services by consumers

classes.name: U.S. producer price index
classes.label: U.S. producer price index
classes.definition: an economic indicator representing a measure of the change over time in the selling prices received by domestic producers for their output

classes.name: urban consumer price index
classes.label: urban consumer price index
classes.definition: an economic indicator representing a measure of the average change over time in the prices paid by urban consumers for a market basket of consumer goods and services

classes.name: urban consumers universe
classes.label: urban consumers universe
classes.definition: a statistical universe for consumer expenditure surveys consisting of people within a household that make joint expenditure decisions

edges.name: has baseline population
edges.label: has baseline population
edges.definition: specifies the starting point statistical universe or population used for comparison or analysis

edges.name: has comparison population
edges.label: has comparison population
edges.definition: specifies the subset of the baseline statistical universe or population used for comparison or analysis

edges.name: has duration of unemployment
edges.label: has duration of unemployment
edges.definition: specifies the length of time, typically in weeks, that people classified as unemployed have been continuously looking for work

edges.name: has indicator value
edges.label: has indicator value
edges.definition: specifies a quantity value for a given indicator

edges.name: has series origin
edges.label: has series origin
edges.definition: specifies the original starting date for the time series for a given economic indicator

attributes.name: excludes energy and food
attributes.label: excludes energy and food
attributes.definition: indicates whether the calculation of the index includes energy and food prices or not

attributes.name: is seasonally adjusted
attributes.label: is seasonally adjusted
attributes.definition: a predicate indicating whether some published formal method is applied that compensates for seasonal variations in the population or index value
